homeCare.title: Home care
homeCare.subtitle: How to care for a dengue patient at home

hydration.title: Hydration
hydration.intro: Drinking enough is the most important home treatment. Sip often through the day, even when not thirsty.

items.ors: ORS (oral saline), made exactly as the packet says
items.soup: Soup, dal water or rice water

fever.title: Fever relief
fever.intro: Use paracetamol only. It lowers fever and pain but does not cure dengue.

items.paracetamol: Paracetamol is the only safe medicine for dengue fever and pain.
items.dose: Never take more than the pack says. Adults: no more than 4 g (8 × 500 mg) a day. Children: dose by weight, ask a doctor.
items.sponge: Sponge with normal-temperature water to cool down.
items.rest: Rest in bed under a mosquito net.

avoid.title: Medicines to avoid
avoid.intro: These painkillers can cause dangerous bleeding in dengue.

items.otherNsaids: Other NSAIDs such as diclofenac or naproxen
items.injections: Injections, steroids or antibiotics unless a doctor prescribes them

warning.title: Warning signs: go to hospital
warning.intro: Go to a hospital emergency straight away if you see any of these, especially when the fever goes down.

items.drowsiness: Blood in vomit or stool, drowsiness or restlessness
items.lowUrine: Very little or no urine for 4 to 6 hours

recovery.title: Recovery signs
recovery.intro: Most people get better in about a week. Keep watching until all of these are true.

items.noFever: No fever for 2 days without paracetamol

checklist.title: Prevention checklist

items.standingWater: Remove standing water around the home
items.coverContainers: Cover water tanks, drums and buckets
items.scrubContainers: Empty and scrub containers and flower-pot trays every week
items.clearDrains: Clear roof gutters, drains and old tyres
items.nets: Sleep under a mosquito net, also in the daytime
items.sleeves: Wear long sleeves and long trousers
